questions.stem:
Let $f$ be the function defined by $f(x)=\sqrt[3]{x-1}$, and let $g$ be the function defined by $g(x)=e^{(-2x+4)}$. The graphs of $f$ and $g$ intersect at the point $(2,1)$. Let $R$ be the region bounded by the graph of $f$, the $x$-axis, and the vertical line $x=2$, as shown in the figure.

Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_1^2f(x)\,dx$. Show the work that leads to your answer.

figures.alt: f(x) = ∛(x − 1) rises from (1, 0) (vertical tangent there) through (2, 1); g(x) = e^(−2x+4) decreases from above, passing through (2, 1) and flattening towards the x-axis near x = 3. Region R (shaded label R) lies under y = f(x), above the x-axis, between x = 1 and the vertical segment x = 2 from (2, 0) to (2, 1). Ticks 1, 2, 3 on the x-axis, 1 on the y-axis.
